text.p: Turkey has taken bids for a dollar Eurobond with a 10-year maturity, bankers said on Tuesday.
They said a mandate for the deal, which could be for between $300 million and $500 million, was expected to be awarded soon.
"Turkey's next deal is likely to be a 10-year dollar bond," a syndicate manager at a European bank said.
"Such a deal is feasible for Turkey to do, although $500 million would be the maximum size."
Bankers said spread talk on such a deal would be in the mid-300s basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
Earlier this month a Turkish government official said it planned to launch a Eurobond in late August or early September, followed by another Eurobond three or four weeks later.
The deals would be denominated in dollars or marks, he said.
Turkey has raised around $1.4 billion in the international capital markets so far this year. -- Aline van Duyn, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7748
